[[Mod#Attributes|Cost]] |- | 0 || +10% || 2 |- | 1 || +20% || 3 |- | 2 || +30% || 4 |- | 3 || +40% || 5 |} ==Drop Locations== *An unranked Hornet Strike is given upon completion of [[The Teacher]] Quest. {{DropLocations}} ==Notes== *Base damage bonuses are multiplied against the base damage of the weapon. **For example, a weapon with a base damage of 100 would deal 320 damage when modded with a max-rank Hornet Strike equipped: {{MathText|100 {{mul}} (1 + 2.2) {{eql}} 320}}. *Base damage bonuses are also multiplied against added elemental damage. **For example, a weapon with a base damage of 100, modded with {{M|Deep Freeze}} would deal 190 damage. Adding a max-rank Hornet Strike would apply a 220% damage bonus to both the base and elemental damage, resulting in 608 damage with both mods installed: {{MathText|100 {{mul}} (1 + 0.9) {{mul}} (1 + 2.2) {{eql}} 608}}. *The high effect of Hornet Strike when combined with elemental damage mods makes it a frequent choice for secondary weapons where the goal is to deal as much damage as possible. Hornet Strike is available from the nearly the beginning of the game, making it a reliable mod choice and a good investment of {{Resource|Endo}} during the [[Star Chart]] section of the game. **Although larger buffs (like those created by {{Arcane|Cascadia Flare}} and {{M|Galvanized Shot}}) can outperform Hornet Strike, those won't be available until significant progress into the later portion of the game has been made, and operate via more involved mechanics. *When more than one damage bonus is present, they are merely added together, not multiplied. **For example, a weapon with a base damage of 100 with a max-rank Hornet Strike equipped would deal only a small amount more when {{M|Pistol Amp}} (+27% Pistol Damage) is equipped: {{MathText|100 {{mul}} (1 + 2.2 + 0.27) {{eql}} 347}}. ==Gallery== HornetStrikeModOld.png|Old appearance ==Patch History== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{ver|32.2}} *Fixed Drop Location text overlapping in the Codex when viewing the following Mods: **Hornet Strike {{ver|8.1.3}} *Fixed Hornet Strike not affecting DOT from the Acrid. {{ver|Vanilla}} *Introduced. }} {{DamageModsNav}} __NOTOC__ [[de:Hornissenstich]] [[es:Golpe de avispa]] [[pt:Hornet Strike]] [[ru:Удар Осы]] [[fr:Nuée de Dards]] [[Category:Mods]] [[Category:Pistol Mods]] [[Category:Uncommon Mods]] [[Category:Damage Mods]] [[Category:Madurai Mods]] [[Category:Flawed Mods]] [[uk:Напад шершня]] [[Category:Update 14]]

{{Top|Enemy|Grineer|Grineer|Weapon|Weapons|Weapons}} {{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic}} {{Codex|A powerful mid-range rifle used by Grineer shock troops, the Hind fires in five round bursts.}} The '''Hind''' is a {{Faction|Grineer}} burst rifle used by their [[Elite Lancer]]s. It fires five-round bursts while maintaining a low recoil allowing all rounds fired to land very close to one another, but has poor critical stats. Pressing [[Alternate Fire]] shoots single rounds with higher damage per bullet and critical stats but lower status. ==Characteristics== *This weapon primarily deals {{D|Slash}} damage. *Innate {{Pol|Madurai}} polarity. {{Advantages|class=Rifle|trigger=Burst| *Highest number of shots per burst out of all burst-fire rifles. *Burst-fire has low [[recoil]]. }} {{Disadvantages|class=Rifle|trigger=Burst| *Burst-fire mode: **Tied with {{Weapon|Burston}} and {{Weapon|Kuva Hind}} for the lowest base damage per bullet of all burst-fire rifles. **Linearly less efficient – sometimes a target may only die with six bullets, which requires an entire second burst to be fired. However, this can be circumvented by using the semi-auto single shot. *Semi-auto mode: **Tied with {{Weapon|Kuva Hind}} and {{Weapon|Nagantaka}} for the third slowest [[fire rate]] of all semi-automatic rifles, after {{Weapon|Grinlok}}/{{Weapon|Prisma Grinlok}} and {{Weapon|Kuva Chakkhurr}}. }} {{WeaponComparison|Kuva Hind}} ==Acquisition== The Hind's blueprint can be purchased from the [[Market]]. {{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}} This weapon can be sold for {{cc|7,500}}. ==Notes== *This weapon was introduced in {{ver|9.6}}. *Mods that affect fire rate will also affect the burst rate, making the Hind very deadly with mods that increase the firerate, and even more so with the addition of punch through. ==Tips== *New players who prefer burst fire but cannot afford this weapon's heavy building cost should stick with the {{Weapon|Burston}} until they have enough resources. *The Hind is made significantly better against enemy groups with the addition of {{M|Shred}} or {{M|Metal Auger}}. *{{M|Stabilizer}} effectively reduces the recoil on every burst giving it more pin point precision over long distances or for better headshots. ==Trivia== *The Hind is one of the Grineer weapons to be showcased in the [[Chemical Lab]]. *The Hind probably derives its name from the NATO reporting name for the famous [[wikipedia:Mil Mi-24|Mil Mi-24]] helicopter gunship/troop transport. Other probable sources of the weapon's name include: **A lesser known aircraft, the [[wikipedia:Hawker Hind|Hawker Hind]], is a pre-WWII British propeller driven bomber. **The [[wikipedia:Golden Hind|Golden Hind]], Captain [[wikipedia:Francis Drake|Sir Francis Drake's]] privateer galleon. **A lunar crater named Hind. *The Hind is one of the few Grineer weapons that are not focused on {{D|Impact}} damage, and instead focused mostly on {{D|Slash}}. This makes them the least effective gun unit in the Grineer arsenal at taking down shields and punching through armor, while being better equipped against the [[Infested]] or [[Corpus]] enemies with shields down. ==Media== WHzBfng.jpg|Promotional art for Hind Hind 2.png|Hind in Arsenal Hind 02.png {{VideoGallery |{{YouTube|fXqFDA2ksZI|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|BoT1gPJVbI4|size=300px}} }} ==Patch History== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{ver|25.7}} *Converted materials to PBR on the Hind {{ver|22.12}} *Status chance increased from 10% to 15% (Primary Fire) *Critical chance increased from 5 to 7% (Primary Fire) *Critical chance increased from 10% to 15% (Alt Fire) *Status chance decreased from 20% to 10% (Alt Fire) {{ver|20.0.8}} *Fixed the Hind’s Alt fire not producing bullet holes when fired at the wall. {{ver|20}} *We've added a single-shot Semi-Auto Alt Fire to the Hind that has increased Damage, Critical, and [[status chance]]. {{ver|The Silver Grove}} '''Conclave:''' *Increased damage of Hind. {{ver|18.5}} '''Conclave:''' *Increased the damage of the Hind. {{ver|17}} *Hind now available in Conclave. {{ver|14.0.11}} *Damage multipliers for the Hind normalized (no more arbitrary multipliers). {{ver|14}} *Tweaked the weapon fire sound effects on the Dera and Hind. {{ver|9.6}} *Introduced }}
''Last update: {{ver|22.20.9.2}}''

==Notes==
*Added in {{ver|10}}.
*This Mod reduces or eliminates firing noise. Enemies that are not killed quick enough will still be alerted.
*Shooting a silent Weapon within 6 meters of an enemy or at the terrain near an enemy will cause them to stop and look around, but will not change their actual alert state.
*Applying this Mod on a high damage Weapon (such as the {{Weapon|Latron Prime}}) will make it suitable for stealth combat, making it a decent alternative to a bow.

'''Hollow Point''' is a [[Corrupted Mod]] that increases [[critical multiplier]] while reducing the [[damage]] of [[Pistol]]s.

==Drop Locations==
{{DropLocations}}

==Notes==
*{{M|Target Cracker}} provides the same critical damage bonus without any penalty (although it does have a {{Pol|Madurai}} instead of a {{Pol|Naramon}}, which works with different builds).
*In most cases, this mod will lower average damage. As such, it is not recommended for any gun other than those with a high critical hit rate (such as the {{Weapon|Magnus}}) and only with particular mod setups already in place.
**It is worth noting that modifications to the same stat are additive and as a result Hollow Point's damage penalty is less substantial when placed on a gun already modified with a high-ranking {{M|Hornet Strike}}. In fact, a gun with a maxed rank copy of Hornet Strike will drop from 320% damage per shot to 305% damage per shot, which is slightly less than an effective damage drop of 5%.

==Trivia==
*In firearm ballistics, hollow-point bullets are bullets made with a bore-hole, or a similar design, in their tips. Upon impact, they rapidly deform and expand causing a significantly wider wound channel and depending on the caliber and target, may even come to a stop inside the target, unlike other round types like FMJ (Full metal jacket), which can easily over-penetrate and waste kinetic energy. Hollow-point ammunition is not often or even usually lighter than the FMJ equivalent. Although this is a common misconception. This mod uses that common misunderstanding to create a more balanced mod with some real world flavor.

The '''Hikou Prime''' is the [[Prime]]d variant of the {{Weapon|Hikou}} throwing stars, featuring higher damage, [[status chance]], magazine, and faster [[reload speed]], at some expense to [[fire rate]]. It was released alongside {{WF|Nyx Prime}} and {{Weapon|Scindo Prime}}.

This weapon can be sold for {{cc|5,000}}.

==Characteristics==
*This weapon deals primarily {{D|Puncture}} damage.
*Works well with {{M|Concealed Explosives}}, considering its high fire rate and ammo capacity.
*Innate two {{Pol|Madurai}} polarities.

{{Advantages|
*Second highest [[fire rate]] of all throwing-type secondaries, behind normal {{Weapon|Hikou}}.
*Fastest [[reload speed]] of all throwing-type secondaries.
*[[Silent]].
*Pinpoint [[accuracy]].
}}

{{Disadvantages|
*Second lowest base damage of all throwing-type secondaries, after {{Weapon|Hikou}}.
*Projectiles have travel time with arcing.
*Very low ammo efficiency.
}}

{{WeaponComparison|Hikou}}

==Acquisition==
Unlike most Prime gear, Hikou Prime is permanently unvaulted, with relics being obtainable through [[Abandoned_Derelict_Caches|Abandoned Derelict Caches]] in Corpus [[Railjack]] missions.
{{PrimeTable}}
{{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}}

===Vaulted===
*On [https://warframe.com/news/last-chance-for-nyx-prime-relics August 9th, 2016], it was announced that Hikou Prime, alongside {{WF|Nyx Prime}} and {{Weapon|Scindo Prime}}, would enter the [[Prime Vault]] and be retired from the reward tables on August 23rd, 2016. Any preexisting components, relics or fully-built weapons will remain as is.
*Hikou Prime, {{WF|Nyx Prime}}, and {{Weapon|Scindo Prime}} can occasionally be acquired via [[Prime Resurgence]], in addition to having their relics obtainable as part of the aforementioned [[Railjack]] missions.

==Tips==
*Make sure to adjust your aim for moving targets, both vertically and horizontally.
*Combining both Pistol Multishot Mods, ({{M|Barrel Diffusion}} and {{M|Lethal Torrent}}), as well as the [[Corrupted Mods|Corrupted Mod]], {{M|Magnum Force}}, allows for easier barrages against mobile/running Targets.
*When using at a distance, aim above the enemy to adjust for Hikou Prime's arc.
*High proc rate means that {{D|Cold}} mods are more likely to slow enemies, making them easier to hit with further attacks.
*Using a {{M|Pistol Ammo Mutation}} or {{M|Primed Pistol Ammo Mutation}} mod can help regain lost ammo when needed.
**Alternatively, bring along a [[Squad Ammo Restore]] or use a [[Carrier]] with {{M|Ammo Case}}.

==Bugs==
*As with all thrown sidearms, when performing a Jump Kick your frame will hold the Hikou Prime as dual pistols. Upon hitting the ground and sliding, this will quickly switch back to as it should be.

==Trivia==
*Hikou (Hikō or 飛行 ) in Japanese means "flight."
*The Hikou are based off the Japanese throwing stars from ninjutsu tradition. Throwing stars were primarily used as distractions, and were often called the "invisible blades" due to a thrown star being able to cut enemies unseen from any direction.

==Drop Locations==

==Notes==
*'''Hydraulic Crosshairs''' is additive with similar mods. For example, a {{Weapon|Sicarus}} with a max rank '''Hydraulic Crosshairs''' and {{M|Pistol Gambit}} will have a {{Math|16% {{mul}} (1 + 135% + 120%)|t=y|p=y}} critical chance.
*Hydraulic Crosshairs will trigger upon weak points, i.e. any weapon hit to an enemy's head, whether the target survives or not.
**weak points will refresh Hydraulic Crosshairs' timer.
*If activated, Hydraulic Crosshairs will display an icon timer beside the player's health UI, and the Warframe will be briefly surrounded by an energy ribbon.
*Hydraulic Crosshairs' buff does not seem to multiply prior flat-crit% buffs such as {{Arcane|Arcane Avenger}}.

==Tips==
*This mod is best used on full-auto pistols with high critical stats, such as the {{Weapon|Aksomati}}, as their high rate of fire ensures that they have a better chance of landing weak points against enemies.
*Can be combined with {{M|Primed Pistol Gambit}} for a total increase of '''+322%''' after getting a shot to an enemies' head. This allows the {{Weapon|Akmagnus}}, {{Weapon|Lato Vandal}}, {{Weapon|Lex Prime}}, {{Weapon|Spira}}, {{Weapon|Spira Prime}}, {{Weapon|Pandero}}, {{Weapon|Plinx}} and {{Weapon|Twin Grakatas}} to gain a [[critical chance]] of over '''100%''' after performing a weak point, allowing orange crits.

==Notes==
*Ideal on weapons with high {{Stat|Critical Chance}} and low [[Status Chance]] such as the {{Weapon|Lenz}}, in order to help it scale better against [[armor]]ed targets.
*Pure [[Elemental Damage|elemental]] weapons such as {{Weapon|Synapse}} can trigger {{D|Slash}} procs using this mod.
*On direct hit, AoE weapons can potentially trigger Hunter {{M|Hunter Munitions}} twice, once on direct impact and an another on the AoE component.
*Works with [[Exalted Weapon]]s such as {{A|Artemis Bow}}.
*{{D|Slash}} proc damage scales with damage multipliers. As such, [[Headshot]]s, orange and red [[Critical Hit]]s will greatly increase the damage dealt.
**As with all {{D|Slash}} procs, their damage only depends on the weapons modded base [[Damage]] and is therefore ''not'' affected by elemental and physical damage mods.
*{{D|Slash}} is affected by status duration mods. Using {{M|Hunter Track}} in tandem with {{M|Hunter Munitions}} will increase the base 6-second duration to 11.4 seconds, allowing for 11 ticks of damage rather than the normal 6 ticks.
*The 30% trigger chance is independent to itself and is '''not''' affected by the weapon's [[Status Chance]], or damage type distribution, besides being indirectly affected by its {{Stat|Critical Chance}}.
*Cannot produce multiple procs in a single instance of damage alongside forced {{D|Slash}} from sources such as {{M|Internal Bleeding}} or the debuff from {{A|Seeking Talons}}, but can stack with {{D|Slash}} statuses applied using a weapon's innate status chance.
**Procs of {{M|Hunter Munitions}} and {{M|Internal Bleeding}} are drawn independently, and if both proc at the same time, only 1 slash proc is applied. With both mods, if a shot both crits and applies impact status, the probability of {{D|Slash}} proc is {{text||54.5%|hover= 0.35*0.3 + (1-0.35)*0.3 + 0.35*(1-0.3) = Probability of both + Probability of only Hunter Munitions + Probability of only Internal Bleeding}} (with attack speed > 2.5) or {{text||79%|hover=0.70*0.3 + (1-0.70)*0.3 + 0.70*(1-0.3) = Probability of both + Probability of only Hunter Munitions + Probability of only Internal Bleeding}} (with attack speed <= 2.5).

==Tips==
*Combining this mod with {{M|Concentrated Arrow}} will allow the arrow's explosion to proc deadly {{D|Slash}} procs for potentially more than 3,500 {{D|True}} damage per tick.


==Trivia==
*Along with {{M|Vigilante Armaments}} and {{M|Hunter Track}}, this is one of the only primary weapon mods that can be used on rifles, shotguns, bows and launchers.

{{Codex|Heat, cold, electricity, or toxin: choose an element and launch a flurry of deadly quills. This versatile sidearm is Khora's signature weapon and has a chance to instantly reload after headshots when she wields it.}}
The '''Hystrix''' is {{WF|Khora}}'s [[Signature Weapon|signature]] sidearm that fires metallic quills. Sporting a high [[critical chance]], it is also a very versatile weapon, with its quills applying {{D|Toxin}}, {{D|Heat}}, {{D|Electricity}}, or {{D|Cold}} elemental status procs that can be cycled at will with [[Alternate Fire]]. In Khora's hands, the weapon has a chance on headshots to instantly refill magazine.

This weapon can be sold for {{cc|2,500}}.

==Characteristics==
*[[Alternate Fire]] cycles between {{D|Toxin}}, {{D|Heat}}, {{D|Electricity}}, or {{D|Cold}} elemental quills. Quills apply a guaranteed [[Status Effect|proc]] of the selected element.
*On kill, bodies will follow the quill that killed them, damaging anyone in their path and pinning the corpse to walls.
*Has an '''8%''' chance to instantly reload on headshots when wielded by {{WF|Khora}}/{{WF|Khora Prime}}.
*Innate {{Pol|Madurai}} polarity.

'''Advantages:'''
*High [[critical chance]].
*Above average [[critical multiplier]].
*High [[fire rate]].
*Fairly quick [[reload speed]].

'''Disadvantages:'''
*Low [[status chance]].
*Small magazine size.
**Coupled with its high [[fire rate]], results in frequent reloading.
*Projectiles have travel time.

{{WeaponComparison|Hystrix Prime}}

==Acquisition==
The Hystrix's blueprint can be purchased from the [[Market]].

{{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}}

==Notes==
*Using the [[Alternate Fire]] button will cycle between the four quill types, each quill characterized by the four main elements ({{D|Toxin}}, {{D|Heat}}, {{D|Electricity}}, {{D|Cold}}). The selected quill will proc the element of its name. For example, the Poison Quill will deal 36.1 base physical damage and proc {{D|Toxin}}.
*The Hystrix by default does not deal any elemental ''damage'', only elemental procs.
*Quill elements are not affected by elemental mods of different elements. For example, using {{M|Jolt}} with the Fire Quill will not combine to either deal {{D|Radiation}} damage or a Radiation proc, even when both the {{D|Heat}} and {{D|Electricity}} procs occur simultaneously.
**However, elemental mods of the ''same'' type will combine. For example, using {{M|Scorch|Scorch}} with the Fire Quill will add to the guaranteed {{D|Heat}} proc's damage over time as if Scorch were a base damage mod.
***Elemental mods of the same type will still combine even when paired with a different elemental mod too. For example, using {{M|Scorch|Scorch}} ''and'' {{M|Jolt}} with the Fire Quill will add to the guaranteed {{D|Heat}} proc's damage over time as if Scorch were a base damage mod, though Jolt will '''not''' be factored into the damage.

==Tips==
*Because elemental mods are not combined with the quill's element, this weapon synergizes well with {{M|Condition Overload}} and {{M|Galvanized Shot}}, allowing players to potentially get up to '''9''' separate proc types on a target (three physical damages, four primary elements, and two secondary elements).
**This can be further improved by incorporating elemental weapons like a {{Weapon|Zenistar}}'s disc, or {{Weapon|Torid}}'s gas clouds to provide the remaining secondary elements.
*Using {{M|Augur Pact}} over any of the +90% elemental mods may be preferable, when expecting to use several of the weapon's elemental effects.
**The former will increase the weapon's physical base damage types, ''and'' the damage-over-time component of its {{D|Toxin}}, {{D|Heat}} or {{D|Electricity}} status effects.
**The latter will add its elemental damage type to ''all'' hits, but any damage-over-time effects from the primary elemental procs, will ''only'' be boosted when they match the elemental mod's type.
**It should be noted that, while the bonus given by both mods seems the same, the elemental damage mods will give much more benefit, as Augur Pact does the calculation alongside base damage mods (e.g. {{M|Hornet Strike}}), while the +90% elemental mods perform the calculation after base damage mods. This can be a significant deciding factor when trying to maximize damage output.
*Greatly synergizes with {{Arcane|Cascadia Flare}}, as the {{D|Heat}} Quill's guaranteed procs will rapidly build up Flare's stacks.

==Trivia==
*''[[wiktionary:hystrix|ὕστριξ (Hystrix)]]'' is Ancient Greek for porcupine.
*The quills fired by Hystrix are not affected by energy color, instead using a different color depending on the chosen quill type. 
*Each quill type has a different visual effect. Fire quills emit bright orange sparks and leave a trail of smoke. Electric quills emit blue sparks and have an arc of lightning that follows them through the air. Ice quills leave a faint blue trail that lingers briefly before fading, and emit light blue particles that dissapear quickly. Poison quills leave an effect similar to heat distortion in the air and emit green particles.
